target.title: fix(copilot): clean up polling abort listeners
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where GitHub Copilot device-code OAuth polling would leave abort listeners on a shared `AbortSignal` after each successful sleep. `once: true` only removes the listener when abort fires, so normal multi-round `authorization_pending` polling accumulates closures and can trigger EventTarget listener leak warnings.

## Why This Change Was Made

`abortableSleep` in the Copilot OAuth helper now settles once on either timer resolve or abort: clear the timer, remove the named `onAbort` listener, then resolve/reject. Already-aborted signals reject immediately without registering a listener. Polling intervals and error text are unchanged.

## User Impact

**Before:** Each successful poll sleep left an abort listener on the login cancel signal.
**After:** Resolve and abort both release the timer/listener; cancel still surfaces as `Login cancelled`.

## Evidence

Branch: `codex/copilot-poll-listener-cleanup` | Base: `upstream/main` @ `a5c5e3b713e7c16225394196af2cb37413f6fe22` | Head: `d506c35a6c87` | Node: v24.18.0 — Windows

### Regression tests

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/llm/utils/oauth/github-copilot.test.ts --reporter=verbose

 ✓ GitHub Copilot OAuth abortable polling sleep > does not accumulate abort listeners across authorization_pending rounds
 ✓ GitHub Copilot OAuth abortable polling sleep > removes the abort listener when cancelled during sleep
 ✓ GitHub Copilot OAuth abortable polling sleep > rejects an already-aborted signal without registering a listener

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  20 passed (20)
```

- Multi-round `authorization_pending` keeps active abort listeners at most 1 and balances add/remove counts.
- Abort during sleep rejects with `Login cancelled` and removes the listener.
- Already-aborted signal rejects without registering an abort listener.

### Diff summary

```text
src/llm/utils/oauth/github-copilot.ts       | settle-once cleanup for abortableSleep
src/llm/utils/oauth/github-copilot.test.ts  | fake-timer polling listener regressions
```

What was not tested: full interactive `loginGitHubCopilot` device UI; only the exported `testing.pollForGitHubAccessToken` sleep/abort seam.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** Copilot OAuth poll sleeps no longer accumulate abort listeners on a shared cancel signal after normal (non-abort) wakeups.
**Environment tested:** Windows, Node v24.18.0, worktree `codex/copilot-poll-listener-cleanup` @ `d506c35a6c87`, focused vitest against production `testing.pollForGitHubAccessToken` / `abortableSleep` path.
**Steps run after the patch:**

1. Run `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/llm/utils/oauth/github-copilot.test.ts --reporter=verbose`.
2. Confirm the three abortable-polling sleep cases assert listener add/remove balance, abort cleanup, and already-aborted rejection.

**Evidence after fix:**

```text
 ✓ GitHub Copilot OAuth abortable polling sleep > does not accumulate abort listeners across authorization_pending rounds
 ✓ GitHub Copilot OAuth abortable polling sleep > removes the abort listener when cancelled during sleep
 ✓ GitHub Copilot OAuth abortable polling sleep > rejects an already-aborted signal without registering a listener
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  20 passed (20)
```

**Observed result:** Peak active abort listeners stay at 1 across pending rounds; abort and already-aborted paths leave zero listeners and reject with `Login cancelled`.
**Not tested:** Full interactive GitHub device-code browser UI / live Copilot login against github.com.
